description: Declarative inventory of what github_core v0 collects per repo. Documents the API surface for inspection; the collector engine in v0 calls these endpoints directly. A future refactor may drive collection fully off this manifest. Each source declares the fine-grained PAT `permission` it needs, so the least-privilege permission set is DERIVED from this manifest (provision-github-pat skill), never hand-listed. Each source's `permission` is the canonical GitHub permission triple `<surface>:<key>:<level>`; the least-privilege set for BOTH the fine-grained PAT and the GitHub App manifest is the union over sources, derived rather than hand-listed (req-github-core-app-auth). A source that genuinely needs no triple states why in `permission_not_applicable` — the exemption is declared, never achieved by leaving the field out.

sources.name: owner_repos
sources.description: Scope enumeration (req-github-core-org-scope): every repository under the envelope's `owner` (org first, user on 404), paginated to the end of the Link chain; the run records the count and whether the walk was complete. Skipped when the envelope is repos-only. Since github-core#76 the same payload also mints the neutral git_core__git_repository (forge = host, stable_id = the numeric `id`) linked by HOSTS_REPOSITORY; a payload without `id` mints no neutral repository and the run says so.

sources.name: org_settings
sources.description: The organization's policy block (req-github-core-settings-1), copied VERBATIM under GitHub's key names onto `github_account.configuration`: 2FA requirement, default repository permission, the members_can_* privileges, the security defaults every new repository inherits, web-commit signoff, the plan. `/users/{owner}` answers for an organization with the public half only; the policy half is on `/orgs/{owner}` and arrives only for an owner or an organization-administration reader — so a payload WITHOUT a single policy key is recorded as `settings_observability: public_only`, a refusal as `unobservable`, and nothing is ever defaulted. This is the cheapest third of the BloodHound GitHub corpus: 17 of its 87 saved queries are filters on exactly these keys.

sources.name: org_actions_permissions
sources.description: Which repositories may run Actions, which actions they may use (all / local only / selected) and whether SHA pinning is required (req-github-core-settings-2) — the organization-level ceiling on every workflow's `uses:`. Admin-only: a member token is refused with 403 ("You must be an org admin or have the actions policies fine-grained permission", measured 2026-09-11), and the refusal lands as `actions_policy_observability: unobservable`, never as "all actions allowed". When the policy is `selected`, `/selected-actions` is read for the allow-list; its refusal alone leaves `selected_actions` null.

sources.name: repository
sources.description: Since req-github-core-settings-3 the same payload also fills `configuration` with the repository's settings under GitHub's own key names — forking, archive state, template flag, merge policy, features, topics — and `security_and_analysis`, the admin-only block GitHub OMITS for a non-admin caller: its absence is recorded as `security_settings_observability: unobservable`, never read as scanning being off. When the config layer supplied the identity half, this is the one extra REST call per repository.

sources.name: workflow_yaml
sources.description: Fetched via GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}; base64-decoded inline; in-memory only (req-github-core-workflow-parse-5).

sources.name: jobs
sources.description: Default endpoint returns latest-attempt jobs only (req-github-core-collector-8). /attempts/{n}/jobs is backlog (req-github-core-backlog-run-attempts).

sources.name: runners
sources.description: Requires repo administration scope on the PAT; degrades gracefully on 403 (req-github-core-collector-5).

sources.name: config_layer
sources.description: The configuration layer in one GraphQL request per 100 repositories (req-github-core-graphql-config): repository metadata, rulesets with their conditions and bypass actors, environments, every branch and tag with the commit it points at, and the inlined content of every workflow file. Measured at 64 rate-limit points of 5000 for a 19-repo organization. Field access degrades per-field (GraphQL answers 200 with both data and errors), and each degraded field is surfaced rather than swallowed.

sources.name: refs
sources.description: Branches and tags with the commit each points at (req-github-core-refs), emitted as the NEUTRAL git_core__git_ref (github-core#76): identity is the neutral repository's id + the full ref path, minted by tap_plugin.git_core.identity; DECLARES_REF__git_core from the neutral repository. Arrives inside the config-layer query at no extra request; declared separately because it needs its own permission statement. Contents read is already in the union for workflow file bodies, so this widens nothing.

sources.name: commits
sources.description: The commit at every collected ref's head — its INTRINSIC half as the neutral git_core__git_commit (github-core#76: identity = hash algorithm + oid, one node however many hosts store it; STORES_COMMIT__git_core from the neutral repository, RESOLVES_COMMIT__git_core from the ref). The observed half — resolved logins and the signature verdict — is the `commit_observations` source. A fragment on the `refs` source's target: scalar fields on nodes the config-layer query already requests, measured at rateLimit.cost 1; no extra request, no extra permission.

sources.name: commit_observations
sources.description: GitHub's OBSERVATION of the commit at each ref head (req-github-core-commits): the accounts it resolved author/committer emails to (a login only when resolved; empty is observed-absent) and its signature verification verdict in three states (state / unsigned / unobservable). Keyed per host + repository stable id + commit identity because the verification record is persisted per repository network; OBSERVES_COMMIT → the neutral commit, OBSERVED_IN_REPOSITORY → the hosting record. Same fragment, same request, same permission as `commits`.

sources.name: rulesets
sources.description: Ruleset DETAIL, fetched once per ruleset per run and cached across the repos it protects (req-github-core-rulesets). The config-layer query already says which rulesets apply; this is the only place each rule's PARAMETERS live, including the required status-check contexts a gate view needs. Whether the response carries a `bypass_actors` key is itself the observability signal: GitHub returns it only to a caller with WRITE access to the ruleset, which this read-only credential deliberately does not have.

sources.name: status_checks
sources.path: derived from rulesets (rules[].parameters.required_status_checks) and workflow_yaml (job display names)
sources.description: Required check contexts (req-github-core-status-checks): one node per (owner, context) named by any ruleset's required_status_checks rule, from the REST ruleset detail the `rulesets` source already fetches — so this widens nothing. A ruleset whose detail was refused carries a type-only rule with no contexts; those are COUNTED as not observable and mint nothing, never rendered as a ruleset without required checks. PRODUCES_CHECK is derived toward these nodes from workflow job display names (exact, or the matrix template) when the requirement allows an Actions check; a check nobody requires has no node.

sources.name: environments
sources.description: Deployment environments and their protection rules (req-github-core-environments), delivered inside the config-layer query. The REST `/environments` endpoint documents an Environments permission; the GraphQL path returned them under the permissions already in this union, so nothing wider is requested. `deployment_branch_policy` is NOT available here and is left null (unobserved) rather than defaulted.

sources.name: environment_detail
sources.description: The REST environment behind the config-layer one (req-github-core-settings-4): WHO the required reviewers are (users and teams, with `prevent_self_review`), whether administrators may bypass the protection rules, and the deployment branch policy — the three fields the node has carried as null for want of a transport. One call per environment already observed; a refusal leaves the fields null and stamps `configuration.detail_observability: unobservable`. Reviewers land as data here; the GATED_BY edges the vocabulary names for them wait for the people graph (github-core#111) to give them a node to point at. `can_admins_bypass` is also copied when present but is not declared here: GitHub's published description of this response omits the key while the live API returns it (measured 2026-09-11), so declaring it would fail the conformance lane against a schema that is behind the service.

sources.name: repository_secrets
sources.description: Actions secret NAMES for one repository (req-github-core-actions-secrets). GitHub's secrets API returns names and timestamps ONLY — a secret's value is write-only and no credential can read it back — so nothing sensitive crosses this boundary and none is stored. The names are what make the join possible: a workflow's YAML says which secrets it references, this says which exist, and the difference is a reference that resolves to nothing (the job receives an empty string at runtime rather than an error) or a secret nothing consumes. 401/403/404 records a degradation and yields no nodes, so a credential without the permission reads as NOT OBSERVED rather than as a repository with no secrets. Repository scope is one of three: see `organization_secrets` and `environment_secrets`, which must all be read before a reference can honestly be called unresolved.

sources.name: organization_secrets
sources.description: Actions secret NAMES held at the ACCOUNT, read once per run rather than per repository (req-github-core-actions-secrets). Names and timestamps only, as at repository scope; `visibility` additionally says how widely the organisation shares each one (all / private / selected repositories) and is the blast-radius field. This scope is why the surface cannot be repository-only: measured on this estate, the most-shared referenced names exist at organisation scope and in no repository, so a collector reading repository scope alone would report a dozen workflows as naming secrets that do not exist. A 404 means the owner is a user account, which has no such surface at all — recorded as information, never as a degradation; 401/403 is a degradation and the scope reads as not observed.

sources.name: environment_secrets
sources.description: Actions secret NAMES held by one deployment environment (req-github-core-actions-secrets). Names and timestamps only. Collected per environment already observed on the repository, so it costs one call each rather than a discovery walk. Without this scope every secret a deployment job reads from its environment would be reported as naming nothing — a false alarm on precisely the jobs that hold production credentials. The reference join still cannot see WHICH environment a job selects at runtime when the `environment:` key is expression-driven; a resolved name here means the repository holds a secret by that name in some environment, not that this job will receive it.

sources.name: caches
sources.description: Stored cache entries, most-recently-accessed first (req-github-core-caches). The `ref` is the load-bearing field: it says which side of the trust boundary an entry came from. Capped per repository, with the total reported.

sources.name: artifacts
sources.description: Artifacts a repository's runs uploaded, newest first, with the producing run on each (req-github-core-artifacts). The REPOSITORY listing rather than the per-run endpoint: one call per page instead of one per run, and it carries `workflow_run.id`, which is the UPLOADS_ARTIFACT source. Expired artifacts stay listed with `expired: true` — an immutable event with a retention window (github-core#14, shape C) — so absence from this listing is never read as expiry or deletion. Capped per repository with the total reported. GitHub keeps no record of who DOWNLOADED an artifact; the declared download steps live on workflow_job.configuration.artifact_steps and no download edge is emitted.

sources.name: app_installations
sources.description: Which Apps can reach this account's repositories, and with which granted permissions (req-github-core-app-installations). App-ONLY: a personal access token gets 404, which is one of the two surfaces that make the App the product credential rather than a convenience. Falls back to `/app/installations` — THIS App's own installation, an inventory of one — when the account-wide list is refused, and says which it got, because an inventory of one is not an inventory.

sources.name: app_installation_self
sources.permission_not_applicable: App-JWT-level endpoint describing THIS App's own installations, not a grant over any account's resources. No fine-grained permission triple exists for it, and inventing one would corrupt the derived least-privilege set. Also the fallback when the account-wide inventory is refused, and how the collector learns which installation it is authenticating as.
sources.description: Self-identification and fallback. A personal access token gets 404 here too.

sources.name: installation_repositories
sources.permission_not_applicable: Answered by the installation token about ITSELF: the repositories this installation is allowed to reach. It is the App's own grant, not a permission over the account's resources, so no fine-grained triple applies (as for app_installation_self). A personal access token gets 404.
sources.description: The installation's repository selection, per run (github-core#141): `all` or the exact `selected` ids, with `total_count` reconciled against the walked count. This is the third term of the tombstone candidate rule — fan-out from the account minus observed minus OUTSIDE THE SELECTION — and it is an operation-side fact about this run's reach (dcom:operation), not a configuration of the account. Recorded as INSTALLATION_SELECTION on the run until the collection_scope node (reliability 1b/1c) exists to carry it. PAT-only runs record the selection as `all` (classic) or `unknown` (fine-grained: not introspectable; the falsifier treats unknown as cannot-weigh-in).

sources.name: rule_suites
sources.description: Pushes evaluated against the repo's rulesets, filtered to those that bypassed one (req-github-core-rule-suites). Answers a read-only App with actor names, where the ruleset's own bypass_actors list does not. `time_period` is explicit because omitting it silently means `day`.

sources.name: rule_suite_detail
sources.description: Per-rule evaluations for one suite. The list says a bypass happened; only this says WHICH control was gone around, which is what makes the event a finding rather than a log line.

sources.name: code_scanning_alerts
sources.description: Every code-scanning alert on the repository in every state (req-github-core-code-scanning): what the scanners (CodeQL, SonarCloud, Trivy, anything that uploads SARIF) found, where, and what became of it. `state` is deliberately OMITTED: without it GitHub returns open, dismissed and fixed alerts together (measured 2026-09-09 on unified-systems-com/tap: 1 open + 2 dismissed + 97 fixed in one listing), so one paginated walk replaces three. Each alert lands twice — as this detail node and as the generic compliance_core__compliance_finding github_core mints for it (DETAILS_FINDING joins them; CARRIES_COMPLIANCE_FINDING from the repository, and from the workflow when the alert's path is a collected workflow file). Walked to the end of the Link chain; a capped walk is warned as incomplete. EMPTY MEANS: zero alerts is a fact only when the repository node says `code_scanning_observability = observed`; `not_enabled` means nothing scans this repository (GitHub's 404 `no analysis found`, or a 403 naming Advanced Security), and `unobservable` means the credential was refused — neither is a clean bill.

sources.name: code_scanning_analyses
sources.description: The most recent hundred analyses — one per SARIF upload — so 'did the scanner run on this commit' is a traversal (ANALYZES_REPOSITORY always; ANALYZES_COMMIT only when the commit is in this batch) rather than an inference from the absence of alerts (req-github-core-code-scanning). ONE page, newest first; a pending next page is warned, and absence of an analysis in this batch is not evidence it did not run. EMPTY MEANS the same three things as the alerts source, read off the repository's `code_scanning_observability`. Same permission, same failure posture.

sources.name: dependabot_alerts
sources.description: Every Dependabot alert on the repository in every state (req-github-core-dependabot-alerts): the vulnerable package and the manifest it was found in, the advisory and its severity, the vulnerable range and the first patched version, and what became of the alert. All four states are asked for by name (open, fixed, dismissed, auto_dismissed) because a fixed alert is history and 'no open alerts' is only meaningful beside 'N fixed'. The endpoint is cursor-paginated and rejects a page parameter with a 400, so the walk follows the Link header to its end; a capped walk is warned as incomplete. Each alert lands twice — as this detail node and as the generic compliance_core__compliance_finding github_core mints for it (DETAILS_FINDING joins them; CARRIES_COMPLIANCE_FINDING from the repository, from the workflow whose path is the alert's manifest, and from the github_action whose action path is the alert's package when that action was used in the run). No ecosystem filter: the documented enum has no GitHub Actions value and none has been observed, so every alert is collected and the ecosystems seen are recorded. EMPTY MEANS: zero alerts is a fact only when the repository node says `dependabot_observability = observed`; `not_enabled` means GitHub reports Dependabot alerts disabled for the repository, and `unobservable` means the credential was refused — neither is a clean bill. Actions alerts exist only for version-tag references, never SHA pins, so an absent alert on a SHA-pinned action is no evidence about it.

sources.name: releases
sources.description: Releases newest-first with their assets and the commit each tag resolved to (req-github-core-releases), delivered inside the config-layer query at no extra request. A release is a product of execution riding the declaration transport. Contents read is already in the union, so this widens nothing. Capped per repository; `totalCount` reports what the cap left.

sources.name: packages
sources.description: Packages under the account, one call per package type in GitHub's closed set (req-github-core-packages). NOT observable with the product credential today, and recorded as such: GitHub's OpenAPI description marks every packages endpoint `enabledForGitHubApps: false`; measured 2026-09-02 with an App installation token, `package_type=container` answers 400 `Invalid argument.` while `npm`/`maven`/`docker` answer 200 `[]` — which proves nothing, since the org's ghcr.io images exist and the per-package endpoints return them. GraphQL's `packages` connection is no better (`totalCount: 0`, no error, same org). An empty listing from a credential the description says cannot use the endpoint is unobservable, never zero; only a non-empty answer proves itself. The permission is declared so an operator who re-accepts it is asking for the right thing; a classic PAT with `read:packages` is the credential GitHub documents for this surface and the envelope does not model one.

sources.name: package_versions
sources.description: Versions of one package, newest first, with the container tags pointing at each digest. Capped per package; `version_count` on the package says what the cap left (measured 1,973 on one image). Same App-support caveat as `packages`; the endpoint DID answer an App token for a public package on 2026-09-02, which is recorded as a measurement, not a guarantee.

sources.name: used_actions
sources.description: Actions a declared job calls (req-github-core-actions-used), split out of the workflow YAML the `workflow_yaml` source already fetches, so this widens nothing. One node per action path, shared across the scope; the pin (`declared_ref`, `pin_kind`, `is_pinned`, `resolved_sha`, `resolution`) rides on the USES_ACTION edge. A mutable name is resolved to a tag or branch and a commit ONLY when the action's own repository is inside the observed scope, from the `refs` source already in hand; otherwise the edge says `unresolved` / `unobservable` rather than guessing. No call is made to an out-of-scope action repository.

sources.name: action_ref
sources.description: Resolves a `uses: owner/repo@ref` whose repository is OUTSIDE the scope to the commit it points at (req-github-core-actions-used-6): `tags/{ref}` first, then `heads/{ref}` on 404, so the pin kind is OBSERVED rather than guessed. Public repositories answer any credential; a refusal lands as `resolution: unobservable` on the edge, never as a missing SHA. At most one lookup per distinct (repository, ref) per run, under a resolution cap. In-scope repositories resolve from the config layer at no request.

sources.name: action_tag_object
sources.description: Peels an ANNOTATED tag to its commit: `git/ref/tags/{ref}` returns the tag object's SHA for an annotated tag, and that SHA is not the commit a runner checks out. One extra call, only when the ref's object type is `tag`.

sources.name: custom_property_schema
sources.description: The organization's custom-property DEFINITIONS, one node each (req-github-core-custom-properties). Read once per run after the repository walk. Organizations only: a user account has no schema endpoint and the surface is skipped, not degraded. A refusal marks every collected repository's `custom_properties_observability` as `unobservable`.

sources.name: custom_property_values
sources.description: Every repository's custom-property VALUES in one paginated listing, stamped onto `github_repository.custom_properties` keyed by property name, built over the declared names first so a declared-but-unset property lands as null (req-github-core-custom-properties). The listing reports each declared property per repository with `value: null` when unset (measured 2026-09-08 on unified-systems-com).

sources.name: pull_requests
sources.description: Pull requests per repository from a GraphQL query of their own (five repositories a page: the config layer is within 40k of GitHub's 500k-node ceiling, and a larger page hits the ~10 s execution limit), most recently updated first, capped with the total reported (req-github-core-pull-requests). The node is github_core's; `PROPOSES_REF` / `TARGETS_BASE_REF` / `PROPOSES_COMMIT` point at git_core's neutral ref and commit, `OPENS_PULL_REQUEST` at the author. A degraded field marks the repository `pull_requests_observability = unobservable`.

sources.name: pull_request_checks
sources.description: The head commit's check rollup — GitHub's combined verdict and the itemised check RUNS (Checks API: GitHub Actions and most Apps) — flattened onto the pull request as `checks_rollup_state` / `checks` (req-github-core-pull-requests). A head with no rollup is `""`, never SUCCESS.

sources.name: pull_request_statuses
sources.description: The other half of the same rollup: commit STATUSES, the older API that Codacy, SonarCloud and other third parties still post and that a required check may be. Same list, `kind: status`; the creator login stands in for the App slug the Checks API would carry.

edges.condition: job.runner_id matches runner.runner_id
job.needs names another job in the same file
git_core-owned edge type; emitted by this collector for every observed ref
the ruleset's include/exclude ref patterns matched a ref observed in this collection
an actor GitHub actually disclosed; see req-github-core-rulesets-bypass
job.environment matches environment.name
cache.ref matches an observed git_ref.ref
run.head_branch == release.tag_name (tag_ref) or run.head_sha == release.target_sha (same_commit); runs with event == release excluded
refs/tags/<release.tag_name> is an observed git_ref
a step's `uses:` names a non-local action; one edge per (job, action, declared ref)
a job-level `uses:` names a workflow file that is on the grid (post-pass over the whole scope); an unresolved call is recorded on the job as `call_resolution`
the target's `on.workflow_run.workflows` names the source's display name, same repository only; an unmatched name is recorded on the target as `trigger_resolution`
artifact.workflow_run.id names a run in the same batch; otherwise counted as unlinked
git_core-owned; the ref's head commit carried a commit slice in the config layer
a required_status_checks rule with parameters on the ruleset detail
a declared job's display name equals a required context (or is its matrix template) and the requirement's integration is null or GitHub Actions (15368)
link_kind owner always; link_kind repository when GitHub links the package to a collected repository
a container tag sha-<short> (or full sha) matches a collected run's head_sha
the repository payload carried a numeric `id`
git_core-owned; one per commit observed at a ref head in this repository
the author is a Bot actor: its login is the App's slug
compliance_core-owned edge type; one per code-scanning alert and one per Dependabot alert, always

compliance_core-owned; the alert's most_recent_instance.location.path (code scanning) or dependency.manifest_path (Dependabot) equals the path of a workflow collected in this run for the same repository

compliance_core-owned; a Dependabot alert whose dependency.package.name is the action path of an action used by a workflow collected in this run. A pip or npm package never matches, so it lands with the repository edge only
always; the alert is the evidence behind the substrate finding github_core minted for it
always; the Dependabot alert is the evidence behind the substrate finding github_core minted for it
the analysis's commit_sha names a commit emitted in this run (a ref head); otherwise no edge and the sha stays on the node
